The ratio loss is an auxiliary loss that penalizes deviations from a target compression ratio 𝑁, defined as 𝐿 Lratio = 𝑁 ((𝑁 − 1)𝐹𝐺 + (1 − 𝐹 ) (1 − 𝐺)) . [HNET §2.2.3 Ratio Loss, p.8]
It is needed because, without it, the model could either keep almost all vectors or compress too much, harming performance . [HNET §2.2.3 Ratio Loss, p.8]
The loss drives the model toward the desired ratio by aligning the fraction of selected vectors 𝐹 with the average boundary probability 𝐺, reaching a minimum when 𝐹 = 𝐺 = 𝑁1 . [HNET §2.2.3 Ratio Loss, p.8]
